subject: Order form DPA: data locality, SCCs, and operational runbook

Subject: DPA / order form — data residency and SCCs questions

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and procurement asked us to follow up with a couple of asks before we can move to signature on the Order Form + MSA:

1) We need explicit language confirming data residency for EU customers and whether any KV cache or prefixing could cause tokens or request-derived data to be stored outside the EU.
2) We require confirmation that Redwood will execute SCCs (the version attached) and whether any delegation (processor->subprocessor) will be noted in an addendum.
3) Procurement wants an evidence packet (SOC2 + latest pen test summary) and a rough runbook for how transfer-impact addenda would be applied in the live environment.

Attached is a short redline from our counsel — we highlight the residency paragraph and a carveout question on caching. Can you confirm operations and legal can sign off or propose alternative language?

Target timeline: we are aiming to sign within two weeks if the residency/caching language is resolved.

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@novafirm.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA / order form — proposed redline and SCCs acceptance

Hi all —

Thanks for the note and the redline, Emily. I reviewed Novafirm’s edits and drafted a single-statement option that we can accept without changing the rest of the MSA: see attached redline (novafirm-dpa-redline.docx) and a short SCCs matrix. Key points below:

- Data locality: Redwood will route and store customer-generated inference inputs, outputs, and associated metadata in the customer-selected region (EU) for accounts that opt into EU residency. We will not persist KV cache entries to storage outside the selected region. Operational ephemeral caches (in-memory on GPU nodes) may exist transiently in the serving cluster for efficiency, but they are not durable storage and will not be part of customer-export artifacts. Suggested contractual language: "Redwood will process and store Customer Personal Data in the region specified in the Order Form. Redwood shall not write durable KV cache artifacts outside the region specified in the Order Form; ephemeral in-memory caches used for inference optimization are transient and controlled by Redwood with a maximum retention of X hours unless otherwise agreed."

- SCCs & delegation: we will execute the current SCC annex as attached. For subprocessor delegation we will include a succinct schedule (exhibit) listing major subprocessors and a clause obligating notice + opportunity to object for material changes. We are not offering per-subprocessor contractual redlining, but we will provide the delegation roster and evidence on request.

- Evidence & runbook: attached I am including a compact runbook outline (kv-cache-runbook-draft.md) that covers: how cache scoping is implemented, TTL defaults, emergency purge steps, and a contact for on-call ops. I also linked our SOC2 report (drive link above) and can provide the most recent pentest summary once the NDA/evidence request tracker is in place.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood accepts the single-statement locality language above and we insert it into the DPA.
2) Novafirm confirms whether the proposed max retention window (we used 24 hours in the draft) is acceptable or requests a different TTL.
3) Ops (Ben) to confirm whether the purge and emergency procedures are operationally realistic and provide estimated cost/impact for pinning.

Emily — if that approach is acceptable we can prepare a redline for execution and a short addendum listing the SCCs and the delegation schedule.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@novafirm.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA / order form — ops confirmation on cache behavior

Short ops note:

- KV cache: our inference runtime keeps per-request KV material in in-memory caches on the serving nodes. Those caches are ephemeral by design and are not durably written to cross-region object stores unless an explicit export job is run.
- Pinning to region: we can pin customer traffic to EU-only serving pools (Dedicated or VPC) which guarantees locality for both memory-resident caches and any short-term spill-to-disk during autoscaling events. Pinning requires a Dedicated capacity reservation or Private deployment (VPC); there is a small monthly surcharge for pinned capacity.
- Estimated impact: for a standard shared-hosting account, scoping caches to EU-only reduces autoscaling flexibility and could increase tail latency during large bursts; minimal cost uplift estimated at ~8-12% on token cost for a pinned pool vs shared routing. For order form: we can add an optional checkbox to request Region-Pinning (EU) with the surcharge and service-level note.

I will add a short ops section to the runbook with purge steps and a timeline for emergency purge (typical RTO ~5-15 minutes depending on cluster size).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call with Novafirm ops to walk through the runbook and the cost tradeoffs.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
